target_near_constancy.method: final_terrain_loss is the mean over the collection series of ((w_harm - target)^2 + (w_goal - target)^2)/2 with targets in {0.2, 0.8}. For an effectively-constant output (independently established by the w_*_std figures above), the best achievable MSE is the target's own variance p(1-p)*0.36 where p is the target switch rate. Inverting the observed losses bounds p.
target_near_constancy.implied_bound: Across all nine cells the terrain-precision target switched state on at most ~2.1% of collection steps, and in the tightest cells (A1/A2 seed 42) on roughly 3 steps in 100,000.
target_near_constancy.consequence: hazard_std is 0.19-0.25, so hazard genuinely varies -- but it essentially never crosses the 0.3/0.33 thresholds that turn hazard variation into a TARGET contrast. The terrain head faced a near-constant target, learned the constant (which is why the loss is tiny AND the output is flat -- the same fact twice), and had no gradient pressure to differentiate by context. The driver's docstring already flagged the neighbouring version of this: it 'corrected' EXQ-194's inherited 0.1 threshold, which 'nearly never fires at this env's hazard-field floor of ~0.22'. The correction moved the target from almost-never-firing to almost-always-firing; it did not make it bimodal.
target_near_constancy.scope_caveat: The bound is derived from the COLLECTION series, which is exactly the series r_w is computed over, so the measurement conclusion is direct. Extending it to the P0a/P1 TRAINING series is an inference (same env, same thresholds, same compute_terrain_loss), corroborated by the terminal near-zero w_*_std. A redesign should measure training-side target balance rather than inherit this inference.

granularity_debt_trigger.basis: granularity_debt_cluster.py MECH-152 reports 1 target across 1 file, alignment distribution other=1 (free-text). The reader correctly declines to assert a clear on free text, so the string was read: it asserts 'aligned -- the run's design maps 1:1 onto each claim's stated mechanism at each claim's own pre-registered granularity', i.e. alignment, NOT weakening. NO target reads `weakened`, which per the skill's own rule is decisive regardless of count: a cluster with no weakened target is measurement or implementation debt, not granularity debt -- exactly this autopsy's conclusion. This is the second autopsy circling MECH-152 and the second signature differs structurally (922: clean falsification under the production combo; 922a: instrument inadequacy), but the second signature is itself measurement debt and this autopsy's own claim_alignment reads `unclear -- untested`, not `weakened`. /claim-synthesis is NOT recommended.

targets.node_classification_basis: The data that settles what went wrong is already in the manifest -- w_harm_std, w_goal_std and final_terrain_loss are unambiguous. The frame (Pearson r over a near-constant target) is what is wrong. More runs of the same design settle nothing; the repair is a re-operationalisation of the DV plus a fix to the target distribution.
learning_extracted: A scale-invariant DV cannot adjudicate a magnitude claim. Pearson r discards exactly what MECH-152 asserts. Whenever a claim states a target band (here w_harm > 0.8, w_goal < 0.5), the primary criterion must be stated on that band, not on a correlation with it.

A non-degeneracy floor is only a guard if it is referenced to the claim's own asserted magnitude. A 1e-9 floor on a [0,1] sigmoid output passed a signal ~1.6 million times below the claimed swing while reporting criteria_non_degenerate: true. Floors set to catch arithmetic degeneracy (pearson_r()=0 artifacts) do not catch functional degeneracy, and the manifest field name does not distinguish them.

Verdict-label branch sets must include the control arm. Declaring a control 'context, not adjudication-gating' is defensible for refusing to VACATE a contrast, but it also means no branch can fire when the control INVERTS the reading. 922a's five pre-registered branches cover A2-vs-A1 exhaustively and the control not at all, so the one outcome that actually occurred is unrepresentable.

A load-bearing premise cleared by a majority-order statistic should report its scatter. The reported `measured` was the median; the mean, the SD and the fact that 1 of 3 seeds violated the bound were all recoverable but none surfaced at the precondition. A load-bearing precondition whose margin is 0.39 SD is indistinguishable in the manifest from one whose margin is 5 SD.

A recovery margin calibrated from a PRIOR run's arm gap inherits that arm's validity. RECOVERY_MARGIN=0.15 was grounded in V3-EXQ-922's ~0.35 A0-vs-A1 gap -- the arm now shown to be the least functionally modulated of the three. Recovery margins should be referenced to the CURRENT run's across-seed scatter, which here would have refused the label (0.184 < 0.193).

A 'diagnostic PASS = the probe ran' convention needs the label to be trustworthy. The convention is honest and worth keeping, but it moves the entire epistemic load onto interpretation.label; when the label's decision rule omits an arm that inverts it, the PASS becomes a certificate of readiness attached to an unsound verdict, and nothing in the indexer's flag vocabulary catches that.

A threshold 'correction' can move a target from almost-never-firing to almost-always-firing without ever making it bimodal. EXQ-194's 0.1 threshold 'nearly never fires'; 194a's 0.3/0.33 correction now fires ~98-100% of the time. Target thresholds inherited as absolute constants should be replaced by thresholds derived from the run's own distribution, and gated by an explicit target-balance precondition.

Recording optional readouts that no criterion consumes is what made this adjudication possible. w_harm_std / w_goal_std / hazard_std / final_terrain_loss are the entire evidentiary basis of this autopsy and none of them is scored. This is the positive counterpart of recording-debt and should be the family default (Experimental Recording Standard, family-keyed payload).

routing_detail.reason: The scientific question changes -- from 'does terrain_weight CORRELATE with hazard' to 'does terrain_weight MODULATE at the claimed depth, and is the modulation precision gain or magnitude scaling'. A 922b letter would signal a same-question implementation fix, which this is not. ID allocation is left to /queue-experiment, not assigned here.
redesign_spec: 1. Fix the target contrast first and GATE on it: add a `terrain_target_balance` load-bearing precondition requiring both target states on >=25% of steps each, in the TRAINING and the COLLECTION series. Prefer deriving the 0.3/0.33 thresholds from the run's own hazard distribution (e.g. a median split) over absolute constants inherited from 194/194a, which have now been on the wrong side twice in opposite directions.

2. Score modulation DEPTH as the primary DV: E[w_harm | hazard-gradient] - E[w_harm | resource-proximate], with the claim's own band as the bar (w_harm > 0.8 in hazard context, < 0.5 in resource context). Demote Pearson r to a descriptive secondary readout.
3. Raise the non-degeneracy floor to something functional -- tie it to the asserted swing, e.g. terrain_weight_std >= 0.05 (one tenth of the 0.6 band) instead of 1e-9.

4. Add the precision-gain discriminator MECH-152's own what_would_answer names and no run has ever executed: does high w_harm measurably REDUCE harm-evaluation variability, or only scale its mean? This is the MECH-152-vs-ARC-016 discriminator (both subsumed by ARC-044) and is arguably higher-value than re-testing the correlation.
5. Keep A0_OFF and SCORE it on the mechanism criteria, and carry a verdict branch for 'control outperforms the experimental arms' -- currently a shape the pre-registered branch set cannot express.
6. Keep recording w_harm_std / w_goal_std / final_terrain_loss / hazard_std per cell.

question.title: Does MECH-152's cue-indexed terrain_weight pathway modulate at the depth the claim asserts (w_harm 0.8 vs 0.2), and can a scale-invariant Pearson-r DV over a near-constant terrain target ever answer that?

decision.decision_question: Is MECH-152's contextual precision modulation present at the asserted magnitude, absent, or merely unmeasured?
decision.live_gate: A run that presents both terrain-target states on >=25% of steps each AND scores the between-context mean difference in terrain_weight against the claim's own w_harm>0.8 / w_goal<0.5 band.
decision.distance_phrase: One redesigned experiment away -- the DV and the target distribution both need fixing before any verdict on the mechanism is possible.
decision.observation_bottleneck: The terrain-precision target switched state on at most ~2% of collection steps in every cell of V3-EXQ-922a, and the scoring statistic (Pearson r) is scale-invariant. Both must be repaired before the mechanism question is observable at all.

hypotheses.label: Hard-Gumbel selection suppresses the terrain-precision signal; softening selection recovers it
hypotheses.desc: The V3-EXQ-922 MECH-152 collapse under the production combo is specific to the hard (near-one-hot) selection operator, and soft selection restores terrain content-tracking.
hypotheses.basis: The clean 1-knob A1->A2 ablation does move the DV by +0.184 (harm) and +0.174 (goal). The coupling is real.

resolution.basis: Neither eliminated nor confirmed. The recovery is real in sign but falls below A2's own across-seed SD (0.184 vs 0.193 harm; 0.174 vs 0.193 goal) on n=3, reaches only 37% / 60% of the 194a bar, and is rank-inverted by the tagger-OFF control (A0_OFF r_w_harm 0.356 at w_harm_std ~1e-6). An uninformative run narrows nothing; it surfaces the observation bottleneck recorded on this question.

hypotheses.label: The terrain pathway does not modulate at the depth MECH-152 asserts, regardless of selection operator
hypotheses.desc: The cue-indexed E1 -> terrain_weight pathway is architecturally incapable of (or has not learned) the 0.6-magnitude contextual swing the claim specifies, so no selection operator will recover it.
hypotheses.basis: Observed terrain_weight std is 3.8e-7 to 1.0e-2 across all nine cells against a claimed swing of 0.6 -- 2 to 6 orders of magnitude low, in every arm.

resolution.basis: Directionally suggested by the universal flatness but NOT adjudicable: the terrain target was near-constant (switch rate <=2%), so the pathway was never given the contrastive pressure that would distinguish 'cannot modulate' from 'was never asked to'. Cannot be eliminated or confirmed on this run.

hypotheses.label: The scoring DV (Pearson r between hazard and terrain_weight) is scale-invariant and therefore cannot adjudicate MECH-152's magnitude assertion
hypotheses.desc: Pearson r normalises out amplitude, which is precisely the quantity MECH-152 claims. A correlation over a functionally-constant terrain_weight is arithmetically real and substantively empty.
hypotheses.basis: Established directly by this run's own data: across all three arms the DV is monotonically DECREASING in cue-indexed retrieval selectivity (A0_OFF 0.356 at w_std ~1e-6 > A2 0.185 > A1 0.001), i.e. it ranks the arms in exact inverse order of modulation depth. The non-degeneracy floor of 1e-9 is ~6 orders too permissive to catch this.
hypotheses.discovery_note: Surfaced by this run's own analysis, on a NEW question, so Mode B's same-edit register-and-resolve applies; no discovery_growth_events entry is owed (that path is for growth of an EXISTING question).

resolution.basis: Confirmed but necessary-not-sufficient (met_elimination_bar false): the three-arm rank inversion against modulation depth demonstrates the DV cannot measure a cue-indexed magnitude claim, but confirming the instrument defect does not by itself close the question about the mechanism.

hypotheses.label: The collection and training distribution almost never crosses the terrain-target thresholds, so the mechanism was never under pressure to modulate
hypotheses.desc: hazard varies (std 0.19-0.25) but essentially never crosses the 0.3 / 0.33 thresholds that convert hazard variation into a terrain-TARGET contrast, so the terrain head learned a constant.
hypotheses.basis: final_terrain_loss of 1.0e-5 to 7.2e-3 against targets in {0.2, 0.8}, with an effectively-constant output (independently established by w_*_std), bounds the target switch rate at <=2.1% of collection steps in every cell and at ~0.003% in the tightest. The tiny loss and the flat output are the same fact.

resolution.basis: Confirmed but necessary-not-sufficient. Directly derived for the collection series (the series r_w is computed over); extension to the P0a/P1 training series is an inference from the same env, same thresholds and same compute_terrain_loss, corroborated by terminal near-zero w_*_std. A redesign should measure training-side target balance rather than inherit the inference.
